cue: How do you say same here in one word?

es.meaning: Likewise; ditto — the same applies to me or to this.

bridge.note: One Latin word, borrowed whole by both languages and left almost untouched — which is rare enough to be worth pointing at, since most of what Spanish and Italian share arrived by inheritance and got worn down differently on the way. Here the only thing either language did to it was spelling: Spanish added an accent because its own stress rules demanded one, ídem, while Italian left it bare. Same word, same job, one diacritic of difference.

interference.es_to_it: Drop the accent. Italian writes idem, and Italian does not use written accents on this kind of borrowed word.
interference.it_to_es: Spanish requires the accent — ídem — because the word is stressed on the first syllable and ends in -m, which Spanish orthography marks. Writing 'idem' in Spanish is a spelling error, not a variant.
